question: Why are mean, variance, and standard deviation useful in feature scaling?
direct_answer: They help center features and put them on comparable scales.
expanded_answer: Many ML algorithms are sensitive to feature scale. Subtracting the mean centers a feature, and dividing by standard deviation gives it roughly unit spread, so one feature does not dominate just because it has larger units or magnitude.
common_wrong_ideas: These statistics are irrelevant if the model is neural
